Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] npm postinstall dropper: node.exe spawning shell/script host or detached child (Mastra easy-day-js) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Sapphire Sleet 'easy-day-js' typosquat dependency landed in node_modules (@mastra supply chain) · [LLM] Sapphire Sleet follow-on: Microsoft Defender exclusion added (Add/Set-MpPreference) · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 / second-stage fetch to Sapphire Sleet (BlueNoroff) Mastra infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cross-platform stealer: non-browser process accessing browser credential & crypto-wallet extension stores · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
Sapphire Sleet 'easy-day-js' typosquat dependency landed in node_modules (@mastra supply chain) AIInstallation High
Detects the malicious dayjs typosquat 'easy-day-js' being written into a node_modules tree, the on-disk artifact of the compromised @mastra npm packages. No legitimate project depends on easy-day-js, so its presence on a developer or CI host is a direct indicator of the Sapphire Sleet supply-chain compromise. Rationale: Anchored on the exact typosquat package name 'easy-day-js' inside a node_modules path — corroborated by Microsoft, Snyk, Orca and StepSecurity. The package has no legitimate use, making file-presence near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://snyk.io/blog/a-forgotten-contributor-account-compromised-the-entire-mastra-npm-package-scope/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised-using-easy-day-js • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/144-mastra-npm-packages-compromised-via.html
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher intentionally detonating the IOC in a sandbox/malware-analysis VM
  • Internal threat-hunt repo containing the package name in a test fixture or detection unit-test
  • SOAR/forensic acquisition copying a quarantined node_modules tree to an analyst host
  • A developer who pinned the package while reproducing the advisory
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","malware-lab","detonation") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("test","spec","fixture"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the easy-day-js version (malicious 1.11.22) and identify the parent @mastra package and the repo/CI job that pulled it; check package-lock.json for the transitive path. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any node.exe-spawned detached processes, rotate npm tokens, cloud API keys, session tokens and any crypto wallet seeds touched on that host. 3) Hunt: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for the C2 IOCs (UC3), check Run keys/LaunchAgents/systemd for persistence, and sweep all CI runners and other developer endpoints for the same node_modules path.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\easy-day-js" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/easy-day-js"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\easy-day-js" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/easy-day-js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm postinstall dropper: node.exe spawning shell/script host or detached child (Mastra easy-day-js) AIExploitation Medium
Detects the easy-day-js postinstall hook behaviour where node.exe (the package install lifecycle script) spawns a shell, script host, or a second detached process to stage the obfuscated dropper. Also flags TLS-verification-disable strings (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED) used before the C2 fetch. Rationale: Targets the article's postinstall-hook execution chain (node lifecycle script spawning a dropper) and the explicit TLS-verification-disable behaviour. Note: NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED is often set in-script (env), so the cmdline clause is a bonus — the node→shell parentage carries the primary signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://orca.security/resources/blog/mastra-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1564.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm packages with native build steps where postinstall invokes node-gyp → cmd.exe/powershell
  • Electron/desktop app installers where node.exe orchestrates a child shell
  • Husky/lint-staged git hooks shelling out from node
  • CI pipelines that run node-based codegen spawning curl for asset fetches
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","node_modules\\husky","lint-staged","electron-builder") or FolderPath has "\node_modules\.bin\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree — was the parent node.exe running an npm/yarn install (check grandparent npm.cmd) and was easy-day-js in the dependency set? Capture the child cmdline. 2) Contain: kill the chain, isolate the host, block the C2 IOCs at egress, rotate developer/CI secrets. 3) Hunt: correlate the child PID against DeviceNetworkEvents for connections to the Sapphire Sleet C2 (UC3) and check for Run-key/LaunchAgent/systemd persistence written immediately after.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","curl.exe","node.exe"))
    or ProcessCommandLine has "NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED"
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "node.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","curl.exe","node.exe")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 / second-stage fetch to Sapphire Sleet (BlueNoroff) Mastra infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Detects host connections to the named Sapphire Sleet C2 infrastructure used by the easy-day-js dropper to fetch the cross-platform stealer second stage. Matches the two C2 IPs and two domains attributed to this campaign. Rationale: Uses the four named C2 IOCs (23.254.164.92, 23.254.164.123, teams.onweblive.org, maskasd.com) tied to the dropper's second-stage fetch. Domains like teams.onweblive.org mimic Microsoft Teams, a known Sapphire Sleet lure theme. Hash IOCs available for file-side enrichment. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised-using-easy-day-js
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform or sandbox sinkholing/validating the IOCs (analyst host)
  • Proxy/secure-web-gateway pre-fetch or URL-detonation engine resolving the domain
  • Internal DNS sinkhole resolving the domain to a parking IP (benign post-block telemetry)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("smartscreen.exe","msmpeng.exe") and DeviceName !has "sandbox"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess that made the connection — if node.exe or a freshly dropped binary, treat as confirmed second-stage retrieval. 2) Contain: blackhole the IPs/domains at egress and DNS, isolate the host, snapshot for forensics. 3) Hunt: sweep all endpoints/CI for the same IOCs over 30d, pull any files written by the connecting process and match against the campaign SHA256s, and check for follow-on Defender exclusions and SYSTEM service install (UC5).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")
    or RemoteUrl has_any ("teams.onweblive.org","maskasd.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr in ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123") or Url has_any ("teams.onweblive.org","maskasd.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("teams.onweblive.org","maskasd.com")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cross-platform stealer: non-browser process accessing browser credential & crypto-wallet extension stores AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a non-browser process reading or copying browser credential databases and extension storage — the collection behaviour of the easy-day-js second-stage stealer, which enumerates 166 crypto wallet extensions (MetaMask, Phantom, Coinbase Wallet, Binance Wallet, TronLink) plus browser histories and saved logins. Rationale: Targets the article's described collection stage — harvesting browser histories, saved logins and 166 crypto-wallet extensions (wallet data lives under Chromium 'Local Extension Settings'/leveldb). Scoping to non-browser initiators of these paths catches the stealer without enumerating wallet extension IDs not given in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://orca.security/resources/blog/mastra-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Browser-profile backup/sync tools (e.g. corporate browser migration, GoodSync, Briefcase)
  • Endpoint backup agents (CrowdStrike/Defender themselves, Veeam, Druva) reading profile dirs
  • Password-manager importers reading Login Data
  • Forensic/DLP agents inventorying browser artifacts
  • Developer scripts (node.exe) legitimately parsing local browser state during testing
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","csfalconservice.exe","backup.exe","goodsync.exe","thunderbird.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process and its path/hash — a binary in %TEMP%, %APPDATA% or spawned by node.exe is high-confidence stealer activity; match hash against campaign SHA256s. 2) Contain: isolate the host, force-revoke browser-synced sessions, and rotate all crypto wallet seeds/keys and SSO tokens for the affected user. 3) Hunt: check for outbound exfil to the C2 IOCs (UC3) right after the file access, and look for the same process accessing extension stores across other hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Local Extension Settings\", @"\Extension State\", @"\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Login Data", @"\Web Data")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","firefox.exe","opera.exe","chrome_proxy.exe","msedgewebview2.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Local Extension Settings\", @"\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Login Data", @"\Web Data")
| where not(ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","firefox.exe","opera.exe","msedgewebview2.exe"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Sapphire Sleet follow-on: Microsoft Defender exclusion added (Add/Set-MpPreference) AIInstallation Medium
Detects the follow-on defense-evasion tradecraft Microsoft tied to Sapphire Sleet on Mastra-compromised hosts: adding Microsoft Defender exclusions before deploying the PowerShell backdoor and SYSTEM service. Flags Add-MpPreference/Set-MpPreference calls that register path, process or extension exclusions. Rationale: Maps to the article's stated follow-on activity (Defender exclusions, PowerShell backdoor, SYSTEM service). Add/Set-MpPreference with an Exclusion verb is the precise, high-fidelity command pattern for this AV-blinding step; pivot from confirmed easy-day-js hosts raises confidence sharply. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://snyk.io/blog/a-forgotten-contributor-account-compromised-the-entire-mastra-npm-package-scope/
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT admin or GPO/Intune script legitimately excluding a dev tool, antivirus-heavy build dir or database path
  • EDR deployment scripts setting interop exclusions
  • Backup/imaging software adding its own process exclusion during install
  • Developer adding a node_modules or build-output exclusion to speed up local builds
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","gpscript.exe","tiworker.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the exclusion target — a path under %TEMP%/%APPDATA%/%PROGRAMDATA%, a node.exe path, or the parent being a non-management tool (not Intune/SCCM/GPO) is suspicious; check the parent process and user. 2) Contain: remove the exclusion, isolate the host, and treat as active intrusion — hunt the excluded path for the staged backdoor. 3) Hunt: look for a newly installed Windows service running as LocalSystem (Security 7045 / DeviceEvents ServiceInstalled), a PowerShell backdoor beaconing to the C2 IOCs (UC3), and correlate to a prior easy-day-js install (UC1/UC2).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","Set-MpPreference")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath","ExclusionProcess","ExclusionExtension")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","Set-MpPreference")
| where CommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath","ExclusionProcess","ExclusionExtension")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows

    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access

            - '\pwsh.exe'

            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526") or SHA1 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526") or MD5 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526") or SHA1 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526") or MD5 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "50eae63d3e24be9ca8803f4b5a0408aef97ee3fab7af018d8c2dde7c359edd65", "1d1bf5e8c1539d2f05b1429235b8f4990f87036774be95157b315a7803dd5526"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
